    In a recent development, AAdvantage Business is the name of American Airlines’ business rewards program. This allows you to earn extra rewards in a business account, in addition to the rewards you can earn through your own AAdvantage account. Best of all, you have quite a bit of flexibility in terms of distributing the rewards. Let’s go over the details of how this works.

    In a recent development, the AAdvantage Business program has a pretty straightforward rewards structure, as it rewards members with both Loyalty Points and AAdvantage miles. With the AAdvantage Business program, you earn the following rewards, which will post within 72 hours of an eligible flight:.

    Let me emphasize that business travelers only earn Loyalty Points through AAdvantage Business when the business is at the moment eligible to transfer miles, and that requires either having the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, or having at least five unique travelers who have credited flights to the AAdvantage Business account, totaling at least $5,000 in flight revenue, over the course of a year (the credit card method is obviously easier).

    Just to clarify a few additional points about AAdvantage Business rewards:.

    These rewards are all in addition to the standard rewards that AAdvantage members receive:.

    According to recent reports, if you’re curious about how the AAdvantage Business program works in practice, let me share some screenshots, for those who are more visual. Once you have an AAdvantage Business account, you’ll automatically become the travel manager for the account, and that means you can invite others to join your account (these should be people who work for your company, but there’s no verification process, as far as I know).

    Recent findings suggest that I should also mention that you can designate others to be travel managers as well, so that they can also invite others, transfer miles to people, etc. Travel managers must also be AAdvantage members who are adults and are residents of the United States or Canada.

    Note that AAdvantage Business bookings are limited to one passenger, so if you have multiple people traveling, you’ll need to book as separate reservations. Also, to state the obvious, AAdvantage award tickets don’t qualify.

    While the Loyalty Points from flights will post directly to the AAdvantage account of the member, the redeemable miles will post to the AAdvantage Business program account (the same is true for miles earned on the Citi AAdvantage Business Card). If you want to redeem miles, the only option is to transfer them to individual members, as you can’t redeem the miles directly out of the AAdvantage Business account.

    Recent findings suggest that the process of transferring miles is super easy. You’ll just enter how many miles you want to transfer, and who you want to transfer them to, and then they should post to the AAdvantage account instantly.

On top of that, the program offers an incremental Loyalty Point per dollar spent — that will have no value to some, while it will have significant value to others, depending on the extent to which you’re pursuing status in the coming year.

    Dozens of passengers across two separate transatlantic Condor flights became ill, causing a mass casualty incident response at Frankfurt Airport (FRA), as reported by aeroTELEGRAPH. While this is still being investigated, there’s a theory as to what happened, given what all passengers had in common….

    In a recent development, on Saturday, November 21, 2026, Condor operated two flights from La Romana, Dominican Republic (LRM), to Frankfurt, Germany (FRA). Both flights were operated by the Airbus A330-900neo, with as many as 620 passengers onboard.

    Industry observers note that flight DE3705 took off at 8:03PM on Saturday and landed at 9:23AM on Sunday, while DE3845 took off at 9:14PM on Saturday and landed at 10:35AM on Sunday. The flights had one thing in common, which is that between them, dozens of passengers became ill.

    It has been revealed that the illnesses onboard were so bad that a “MANV 25” response was triggered at Frankfurt Airport. That’s a German emergency response alert for a mass casualty incident — “Massenanfall von Verletzten” (though fortunately there were no fatalities here).

    Passengers onboard were screened by medical teams, and one person on each flight was taken to a local hospital, while others are being monitored.

    Industry observers note that it’s not uncommon to hear stories of multiple people becoming sick on flights. Sometimes it’s a fume event, sometimes it could be a case of food poisoning (though it doesn’t usually happen that fast), etc. So what’s going on here, that people on two separate Condor flights became ill?

    Well, the passengers on these two flights had one thing in common — they all came off the AidaBella cruise ship in La Romana, and then these flights were sold as part of the cruise package.

    Sources indicate that so while this is still being investigated, a norovirus outbreak on the cruise ship is believed to be the likely culprit. I’ve gotta say, an airplane seems like a pretty unpleasant place to come down with a gastrointestinal illness, so I imagine the lavatory situation onboard probably wasn’t great.

    Dozens of passengers on two separate Condor flights between the Dominican Republic and Germany around the same time became ill, triggering an emergency response at Frankfurt Airport, which included a couple of people being hospitalized.

    According to recent reports, while it remains to be seen what caused this, the belief is that it could be some sort of a norovirus outbreak, based on the symptoms, as well as the fact that the passengers had all come off the same cruise ship. I hope everyone makes a quick recovery.

    Qatar Airways Airbus A321LRs With Flat Bed Business Class Launching Soon

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR, which will be the carrier’s first narrow body aircraft featuring latest generation interiors, including flat beds.
    • Qatar Airways at the moment has a total of 50 factory fresh Airbus A321-family aircraft on order.
    • According to recent reports, the expectation is that the first A321LR will be delivered in the coming weeks, before the end of 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR, which will be the carrier’s first narrow body aircraft featuring latest generation interiors, including flat beds. The airline will be introducing a “mini-Qsuite” type product on these planes, and we’ve now learned exactly when this latest premium narrow body jet will enter service.

    Qatar Airways at the moment has a total of 50 factory fresh Airbus A321-family aircraft on order. This includes 10 A321LRs and 40 A321neos — both of those are latest generation aircraft, with the A321LR featuring additional range.

    According to recent reports, the expectation is that the first A321LR will be delivered in the coming weeks, before the end of 2026. The 10 A321LRs should join the fleet pretty swiftly, and will then be followed by the A321neos. The A321LRs will be configured with 160 seats, including 16 business class seats and 144 economy class seats.

    The A321LR has a maximum range of 4,000 nautical miles, so it can be used for many destinations in Europe, Africa, and Asia. Below is a map showing the rough range from Doha (though in reality it won’t be quite as far, accounting for winds, fuel reserves, etc.).

    Now, for those paying close attention, I should acknowledge that Qatar Airways briefly flew six leased, all-economy A321neos, but those were just intended as a temporary solution, and are now flying for Sun PhuQuoc Airways, which is running an interesting operation.

    Recent findings suggest that qatar Airways’ A321neo-family aircraft order goes back a long time, and involved a lot of drama. The order was first confirmed in 2011, then the airline reconfirmed and upsized it in 2017. However, then former Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker got into a fight with Airbus over A350 production quality, and refused to take delivery of any Airbus planes.

    Sources indicate that that turned into a massive court battle, which was eventually resolved. But in the process, Qatar Airways lost all of its Airbus delivery slots, which is why these planes are coming way later than initially expected.

    According to recent reports, qatar Airways has been promising all along that it would introduce some sort of a next generation flat bed business class product on its Airbus A321LRs. As you’d expect, business class seats on narrow bodies sometimes differ from those on wide bodies, due to differing cabin constraints.

    What can we expect onboard these Qatar Airways A321LRs in business class? Executive Traveller quotes Qatar Airways CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater as saying that the newly introduced business class product will be based on the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform.

    In a recent development, these planes will boast 16 business class seats, in a 1-1 configuration. This product offers reverse herringbone seats, and Qatar Airways looks to have doors at each seat as well, of course with its customized finishes.

    Recent findings suggest that the launch customer for the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform was Air France on its A350s. However, that’s the wide body version of the seat, which is modified from the narrow body version.

    When it comes to the narrow body version of the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, ITA Airways was the launch customer, on its A321neos.

    Sources indicate that this is also the product that Etihad is installing on its A321LRs. ITA Airways and Etihad don’t have doors in business class, but Qatar Airways does strategy to offer it. Etihad also markets the first row of the cabin as first class (and that has doors), but I wouldn’t expect Qatar Airways to do something similar.

    This is about as good as narrow body business class seats get, as it’s generally preferred to the herringbone seats you’ll find on other carriers, like JetBlue A321LRs, American A321XLRs, etc.

    Qatar Airways now seems pretty certain about the delivery of its upcoming Airbus A321LRs, as the airline has officially put the first routes on sale, as flagged by AeroRoutes:.

    When you pull up the above flights, you’ll now see the seat map for the A321LR, which confirms the 16-seat business class cabin.

    In the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first of 10 Airbus A321LRs. This will be the first custom designed next generation narrow body that the airline takes delivery of. We knew the airline would offer flat bed seats on these planes, and now we have the details of that.

    The airline has gone with the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, the same product you’ll find on similar planes of Etihad and ITA Airways. However, unlike those airlines, Qatar Airways will have doors in business class. The planes will enter service by very early 2027, flying from Doha to both Vienna and Zurich.

    #99863. Why The US Military Is Expanding A Remote Pacific Airport To Reduce Its Reliance On Guam

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1516 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Why The US Military Is Expanding A Remote Pacific Airport To Reduce Its Reliance On Guam

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In October and November, I visited the Micronesian island countries of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM).
    • It has been revealed that when I visited, work on the airport had not yet started, and the US military footprint on the island was minimal.
    • According to recent reports, the knowledge that Yap Island's airport was soon to be transformed was surreal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In October and November, I visited the Micronesian island countries of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM). The FSM consists of four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae. I visited Yap, whose airport is set to receive some major work by the United States to prepare it for war as part of the USAF's broader Agile Combat Employment (ACE) doctrine to disperse aircraft from Guam. Separately, US Navy personnel on the island informed me that there are plans to dredge the island's harbor to allow large warships to berth. Funding has not yet been approved.

    It has been revealed that when I visited, work on the airport had not yet started, and the US military footprint on the island was minimal. The hotel I stayed at houses around half the personnel (mostly US Navy) on the island for periods of six months. I arrived in Yap from Palau, where the minor airfield of Peleliu was closed because major construction work to expand the airport for ACE operations was underway. Here is what to know about the US's looks to expand Yap International Airport to relieve wartime strain on Andersen Air Force Base in Guam.

    According to recent reports, the knowledge that Yap Island's airport was soon to be transformed was surreal. The island is one of the remote islands in the Pacific and is difficult and expensive to reach. Adjacent to the international airport is an old Japanesee WWII airfield littered with aircraft destroyed by American bombing and lost to the jungle. I found around eight Japanese airplanes, some marked, some not marked. Here and there around the islands are the remains of lost US Vought F4U Corsairs and bombers.

    Recent findings suggest that today, the island feels like a world away, but the USAF plans to improve the airports and airfields on the Second Island Chain as competition with China heats up. The echoes from WWII are clear. In 1944, the US island-hopped to Japan to project airpower over the Japanese home islands.

    Now those same islands are needed to project airpower over the First Island Chain. The First Island Chain includes Taiwan, Japan's southern islands, and the Philippines. Following WWII, the US consolidated its airpower and military bases on Guam, while maintaining forward bases in Japan and Korea. The rise of China puts not only those forward bases at risk, but also Guam, which is now a prime target. Without Guam, or an effective alternative, the US's ability to project airpower over the region would diminish drastically.

    Industry observers note that the WWII US invasion of the island of Peleliu was one of the deadliest operations for the US Marines during the Pacific War. Fortunately for the native Yapese, the island was not invaded. Instead, it was intensively bombed, bypassed, and rendered irrelevant. Japanese forces remained on the island until the surrender. Most of their aircraft were destroyed in air campaigns.

    It has been revealed that the Japanese airfield is now abandoned and overgrown, but next to it, Yap International Airport operates. Yap Airport is a simple single-runway airport with a basic terminal building. The only scheduled passenger flights that use the airport are United Airlines and Pacific Missionary Aviation (PMA) United operates 737 MAX 8 flights from Guam twice weekly; this is the primary connection to the outside world. Outside of United's flights, Yap's terminal building is generally closed.

    It has been revealed that PMA operates passenger flights once a week (soon to be twice) from neighboring Palau using its two Super King Airs (seven to nine seats, depending on freight). PMA also operates flights to Yap's outlying islands as well as MEDEVAC and emergency services. I flew the PMA passenger flight from Palau to Yap, was invited on a flight to an outlying island (Ulithi), and flew out on United. PMA operates from its own private hangar and operates domestic flights from there. International (Palau) flights run through the main terminal.

    Funding for Yap Airport's transformation appears in two main categories: civilian FAA Airport Improvement Program (AIP) grants and the Department of Defense/Air Force military construction and related funding. The Air Force's Fiscal Year 2025 Military Construction budget request included around $400 million for runway extension and related work. This is labeled "PDI: Runway Extension, Inc." in the documents. The first increment funding is $96 million.

    A modest reduction appears in Fiscal 2027 documents with the explanatory note, "Program execution encountered delays and slipped from FY2025 to FY2026, funding reflects the one-time decrease after increase to support acquisition of land for an agreed upon defense site under appropriate international agreement required to complete the runway extension, parking apron, and taxiway construction at Yap International Airport, Wake Island.".

    Industry observers note that the decrease is $31 million, but as the note includes Wake Island, it is unclear how much of this is relevant to Yap. The justification language for the funding emphasizes the need for a longer runway and facilities to support larger military aircraft for training, operations, contingency, and Agile Combat Employment. In the event of a high-end conflict with China, this likely means that Yap will be on China's list of strategic targets to be hit and neutralized.

    The United States is currently upgrading numerous airports and airfields across the Second Island Chain as part of its ACE doctrine and preparations to counter China. As stated, one of the most significant programs currently underway is rehabilitating Palau's Peleliu airfield, while Angaur Airfield is already complete. On Guam, the USAF is expanding parking areas on its primary Andersen Air Force Base and rehabilitating its adjacent, formerly abandoned Northwest Field.

    Industry observers note that one of the biggest areas of effort is on the island of Tinian in the Northern Mariana Islands. There, the USAF is expanding and rehabilitating Tinian International Airport and the formerly abandoned North Field. Nearby, the island of Rota (home to fewer than 2,000 inhabitants) has also been an area of interest and increased military exercises. The civil airports on Palau, Saipan, and Guam also factor into US ACE planning, even if no work is being carried out to expand them.

    Select Micronesian airports/airfields being expanded for ACE (per budget documents).

    It has been revealed that one important effort is Australia. Australia is not part of the Second Island Chain, and the relationship with Washington is very different from that of small Pacific islands. In Australia, effort is mostly focused on Australia's northern RAAF bases: Tindal, RAAF Darwin, and possibly RAAF Amberley. These are being prepped primarily for US strategic bomber use with associated aerial tankers.

    Following WWII, the United States occupied the Japanese South Seas Mandate and formally took over administration as the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (TTPI). Eventually, the Trust Territory was broken up. The Northern Mariana Islands joined the United States as a commonwealth, while Palau, the FSM, and the Marshall Islands became independent nations with full United Nations membership.

    However, sovereignty for these islands is nuanced. As part of the process, the newly independent states signed the Compacts of Free Association with the United States. Of interest to this article is that the United States retained responsibility for the defense of the islands. In practical terms, this gives the US military the benefits of basing in US territories without the islands actually being US territories.

    The FSM government states, "Under the Compact, the United States provides financial assistance, defends the FSM’s territorial integrity, and allows FSM citizens unrestricted travel to the U.S. In return, the FSM grants the United States exclusive access to its land and waterways for strategic purposes." The Compact grants the United States "full authority and responsibility for security and defense matters," although in practice, the US extensively collaborates with the government rather than dictates.

    Visiting Yap today, it is surreal to feel so isolated and yet also see the island reprising its role as potentially returning to the frontline of a major Pacific competition. In the years ahead, the airport may start to see the deployment of US tankers and F-35 fighter jets just hundreds of feet (meters) away from the rusting hulks of Japanese Zeros and American Corsairs rotting in the jungle.

    Industry observers note that in WWII, the US Navy drew up a initiative to invade Yap, but this was scrapped in favor of bombarding it and bypassing it. China’s primary counter to ACE is the continued expansion of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force (PLARF) and supporting systems, including large inventories of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and hypersonic missiles. These are intended to hold US airfields at risk across the First and Second Island Chains.

    It has been revealed that the US is aware of this. Increasingly, the US Air Force, Marines, and Navy are focusing on increasing the range of next-generation fighter jets (e.g., F-47 and F/A-XX). Logistics and assault requirements increasingly focus on being runway-independent, with the US Army's incoming MV-75 tiltrotor being an example. The Marines, in particular, are investing in a range of runway-independent and sea-skimming drone options for the 'last mile' of resupply and MEDEVAC.

    Getting a refund for a canceled or delayed flight: What your rights are in 2026

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (165 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • Recent disruptions in U.S. air travel highlight the importance of understanding passenger refund rights.
  • Federal rules require airlines to issue refunds for canceled flights or significant delays if you choose not to travel, regardless of the cause.
  • A 'significant delay' is defined as three hours or more for domestic flights and six hours or more for international flights.
  • Refunds must be processed automatically and promptly—within seven days for credit card payments and 20 days for other payment methods.
  • Refund eligibility only applies if you decline rebooking and do not accept alternative compensation such as vouchers or miles.
  • Airlines are not required to provide compensation for meals, hotels or ground transportation unless the disruption is within their control.
  • Passengers can file a complaint with the Department of Transportation if they believe refund rules were not followed.

  • A detailed breakdown of when to accept miles or vouchers versus a cash refund, and how to assess their value.

    • In May 2026, we saw American introduce a major newly introduced restriction for award travel, which had the biggest implications for those redeeming on American through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club (in other words, anyone redeeming through a program other than American AAdvantage).

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In May 2026, we saw American introduce a major newly introduced restriction for award travel, which had the biggest implications for those redeeming on American through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club (in other words, anyone redeeming through a program other than American AAdvantage).

    It has been revealed that with this, American started to restrict its own saver level award availability close to departure. Initially, all domestic nonstop saver awards within six days of departure were pulled. In recent days, it looks like American has expanded this to all domestic connecting itineraries as well, so I’d like to cover those details (thanks to azbobcat for flagging this).

    Historically, American has been by far the best of the “big three” US carriers when it comes to making award seats on its own flights available, especially on domestic and short haul international flights. American actually releases a good amount of saver award seats across cabins, and it’s one of the things that makes AAdvantage better than the competition.

    However, in May 2026, we saw American introduce a major change to how it releases award space to partner frequent flyer programs. Long story short, American started blocking all nonstop, domestic saver award availability, for flights within six days (exactly 144 hours) of departure.

    As soon as a flight gets to the point where it’s 144 hours until departure, you’ll see that the airline “turns off” its saver fare classes — I’m referring specifically to the “U” (saver business class award) and “T” (saver economy award) fare classes, which show up when searching on ExpertFlyer, for example.

    Recent findings suggest that initially, this applied exclusively to nonstop, domestic award tickets, as connecting itineraries and all international itineraries (including short haul international ones) weren’t impacted by this. However, this seems to have now expanded to domestic connecting itineraries as well.

    It has been revealed that so any wholly domestic itinerary exclusively on American is no longer bookable at the saver level within six days of departure. International itineraries continue to be bookable within six days of departure, whether traveling nonstop or with a connection.

    What would cause American to suddenly “shut off” saver awards for domestic routes within days of departure?

    What’s interesting here is that the implications for AAdvantage members are limited. Yes, American has shut off awards in the saver fare classes, but that’s not to say that American isn’t making reasonably priced awards available within days of departure. American has long used some kind of dynamic award pricing concept for its own flights, regardless of whether or not there’s saver availability.

    It’s just that any awards in the official saver fare buckets aren’t available, and therefore aren’t bookable with points belonging to partner programs.

    Recent findings suggest that so it sure seems to me that the intent here is to block award availability for those booking through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club. It goes without saying that I absolutely hate this restriction, as someone who “funds” a vast majority of my domestic American travel using Atmos Rewards points. At the same time, I also have to say that I can’t blame American for this change, as the airline has just made it too easy.

    Sources indicate that I’ve been booking basically all my travel directly into American first class using Atmos Rewards points — I just set ExpertFlyer availability alerts for “U” class, it opens up a vast majority of the time, and then I book. It’s not surprising that American finally got a bit savvier.

    In a recent development, american is now blocking all saver awards within exactly six days of departure for all domestic itineraries. This means within that timeframe, there’s no “U” or “T” availability, which corresponds to the saver business and economy award fare buckets, respectively. Initially this only applied to nonstop flights, while now it also applies to connecting itineraries.

    According to recent reports, for American AAdvantage members, the implications are limited, since American can still make reasonably priced awards available, just not formally in those fare buckets. The practical implications here are that partner programs just don’t have access to these award seats close to departure anymore.

    What do you make of American’s six day rule on award tickets?

    Breaking: Southwest Airlines Plus Card Review: Modest Benefits For A Low Annual Fee

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2134 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Southwest Airlines and Chase have a great portfolio of co-branded credit cards at a variety of “price points” (and by that I mean annual fees).
    • Industry observers note that in my Southwest Plus Card review, I’ll cover the benefits and explain why now is a good time to consider this card if you want to use credit card spending to earn the Companion Pass.
    • Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines and Chase have a great portfolio of co-branded credit cards at a variety of “price points” (and by that I mean annual fees). In this post, I’d like to take a closer look at the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card, which is Southwest Airlines’ lowest annual fee credit card.

    Industry observers note that in my Southwest Plus Card review, I’ll cover the benefits and explain why now is a good time to consider this card if you want to use credit card spending to earn the Companion Pass. I’ll also explain why other Southwest cards can be better, and share a great alternative to earning Southwest Rapid Rewards points altogether.

    Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card.

    Before I get into my Southwest Plus Card review, here are some of the key card details:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Southwest Plus Card’s pros and cons:.

    Let’s take a look at the Southwest Plus Card‘s welcome bonus, annual fee, and eligibility rules, as these are some of the most important factors to take into account if you’re considering applying.

    The Southwest Plus Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus: Earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. This is one of the higher bonuses I’ve seen on this card recently, making now a particularly good time to apply.

    Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Rapid Rewards points to be worth 1.2 cents each. So to me, the points from this welcome offer are worth $960.

    In a recent development, in terms of Southwest credit card eligibility, the card isn’t available to anyone who right now has a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card, or anyone who has received a welcome bonus on a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card in the past 24 months. However, you are eligible if you have a Southwest business credit card.

    It has been revealed that beyond the restrictions related to which Southwest cards you have, keep in mind the general restrictions for Chase card approvals, including the 5/24 rule. However, there are increasing data points of this no longer being consistently enforced.

    Another rule worth mentioning here involves how Southwest credit card welcome bonuses help you earn the Companion Pass, which lets you bring a companion with you on flights (both cash and award tickets) and pay just taxes and fees.

    Industry observers note that for a long time now, the points earned as part of Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have counted towards the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn the Companion Pass. But starting soon, credit card welcome bonuses will no longer count toward qualification.

    You’ll need to apply for a card by December 2, 2026, for your welcome bonus to count toward the Companion Pass for a final time. So apply for this card now if you’re hoping to earn that perk with the help of credit card spending.

    Now is also your last chance to get an annual boost of 10,000 Companion Pass qualifying points as a Southwest credit card holder. Starting next year, instead of a boost of 10,000 TQPs for having a Southwest card, you’ll get 10,000 TQPs if your TQP balance is 130,000 by December 31, 2027. That would be enough to get you to Platinum status, which will include unlimited Companion Pass trips as a benefit.

    This change eliminates the easiest way to earn this valuable benefit, and it’s not the only new rule: referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending, and partner spending won’t count toward the Companion Pass either. In fact, Southwest’s rolling the Companion Pass into its highest elite tier, Platinum, and requiring either 140,000 TQPs or 100 qualifying flights to earn it.

    The Southwest Plus Card has a $99 annual fee, and you can add authorized users to the card at no extra cost.

    $99 is the lowest annual fee of any Southwest Airlines credit card. Looking at the high end, Southwest’s personal cards have annual fees of up to $229, and Southwest’s business cards have annual fees of up to $299.

    The Southwest Plus Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a solid card to use for purchases abroad.

    As far as the Southwest Plus Card‘s rewards structure goes, the card offers the following:.

    Since I value Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.2 cents each, I think you get an effective return of 2.4% on purchases that qualify for 2x points, and a 1.2% return on everything else.

    It’s nice that the card has some bonus categories, though there are ultimately more rewarding cards out there for everyday spending. Plus, a few of the non-Southwest bonus categories have an annual cap, which limits how useful this card is for maximizing your return on gas station and grocery store purchases.

    I have a dedicated post that covers how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but let’s briefly look at how you can use the points you earn from the Southwest Plus Card.

    Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, meaning that the value you get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. There are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares, so the exact value can vary a bit.

    Recent findings suggest that basic award fares tend to offer the best redemption value. You’ll also usually get the best value on international Southwest routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. I’ve been able to get about 2.0 cents per point on these redemptions.

    Recent findings suggest that starting in spring 2027, Southwest will add points earning and redemption opportunities with select airline partners, which should make your Rapid Rewards points more valuable for international travel. The planned partners include Icelandair, China Airlines, and Etihad Airways — I look forward to seeing how these add value to the program.

    It has been revealed that one great thing about the Southwest Rapid Rewards program is that there are no change or cancellation fees, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d cancel and rebook rather than change.

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Plus Card offers some benefits that could make the card worth keeping long term. However, this is also Southwest’s lowest annual fee card, so it doesn’t have the most benefits. What are the ongoing perks of having this card?

    According to recent reports, the Southwest Plus Card gets the primary cardholder and up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation a first checked bag at no additional cost. Checked bags on Southwest cost $45 each way, so this can save you up to $90 roundtrip on checked bag fees per person. So with just one roundtrip flight per year, this benefit can almost offset the annual fee.

    Southwest now charges for seat selection, so it’s helpful that the Southwest Plus Card includes complimentary standard seat selection starting 48 hours out from departure. This perk is based on availability, and it could save you around $20 to $40 per flight.

    It has been revealed that another Southwest benefit is early boarding. You’ll be able to board with Group 5, or earlier if you have elite status or a fare or seat type that qualifies you for an earlier boarding group. Southwest has eight total boarding groups, so while there are several ahead of Group 5, it’s better than boarding last.

    Industry observers note that each year on your Southwest Plus Card cardmember anniversary, you’ll get a 10% promo code that applies to Southwest flights. Just note that this discount excludes Basic fares.

    On your Southwest Plus Card cardmember anniversary every year, you’ll receive 3,000 bonus points. Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and you’ll typically need 83 Rapid Rewards points for every dollar of airfare you book. In other words, those 3,000 Rapid Rewards points should get you around $36 worth of airfare on Southwest annually.

    Recent findings suggest that as part of an overhaul of the Rapid Rewards program, Southwest is simplifying TQP earning on credit cards. Starting in 2027, every dollar spent on a co-branded Southwest credit card will earn you one TQP. In other words, $35K in spending would earn you Silver, $65K in spending would earn you Gold, and $140K in spending would earn you Platinum.

    This earning rate is the same across cards, so this isn’t specific to the Southwest Plus Card.

    The Southwest Plus Card offers 25% savings on inflight purchases of Wi-Fi and drinks. Simply pay with your card, and you’ll automatically receive a statement credit for that amount.

    The Southwest Plus Card offers a variety of travel & purchase protection benefits, including:.

    You’ll want to check the cardmember agreement for the full terms & conditions associated with these benefits.

    One of the great features of Chase cards is access to Chase Offers, which provides savings on purchases with all kinds of retailers. This program has saved me a significant amount of money.

    The Southwest Plus Card is a solid entry-level airline credit card. If you want a credit card from Southwest and want an annual fee as low as possible, then this card could make sense to you.

    Recent findings suggest that you’ll receive a 3,000-point bonus on your cardmember anniversary every year, and 25% savings on inflight purchases. The free checked bag benefit can save you $90 on a roundtrip and the complimentary standard seat selection benefit can add up swiftly after a few flights. These perks can more than justify the annual fee, and that’s not even accounting for the massive welcome bonus.

    However, there are other options that I think can make more sense.

    According to recent reports, if your main reason for considering the Southwest Rapid Rewards Plus Card is to earn points for Southwest award flights, you might be better off skipping a Southwest co-branded credit card altogether and just earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points. You can transfer Chase points to Southwest to book flights, and cards like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (learn more) have stronger earning categories and benefits overall.

    You can also redeem Ultimate Rewards points with other travel partners, not just Southwest, so this option gives you more flexibility.

    The Southwest Rapid Rewards® Premier Credit Card (learn more) is one step up from the Southwest Plus Card, with a $149 annual fee. Here’s a look at its key perks:.

    There’s also the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (learn more), the most premium personal Southwest card with a $229 annual fee. If you want as many Southwest perks as possible, this is a better pick.

    The Southwest Priority Card’s main perks include:.

    So you’re getting a higher return of 4.8% on Southwest spending on the Priority Card, based on my valuations, and better complimentary seat selection and upgrade options.

    In a recent development, if you want a Southwest Rapid Rewards business credit card in place of or in addition to a personal card, I highly recommend considering the Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card (learn more). The Southwest Performance Business Card offers the following benefits, which make it the best Southwest credit card, in my opinion:.

    The Southwest Performance Business Card offers a lot of points, and more perks overall than other Southwest cards.

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Plus Card is a good entry-level credit card for someone who wants to earn Rapid Rewards points without paying a high annual fee. It’s not the most valuable Southwest credit card in the lineup, but its benefits and strong welcome bonus make it a good option at this price point.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S.
    • That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.
    • “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images).

    That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

    “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

    In a recent development, trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he introduced a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

    “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

    They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

    According to recent reports, his interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

    It has been revealed that both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

    Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

    Recent findings suggest that “I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump stated as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

    In a recent development, “You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”.

    Trump, who was convicted by a Fresh York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

    Industry observers note that “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

    Other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

    And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

    It has been revealed that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of complications, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

    “This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer noted.

    Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”.

    According to recent reports, nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “key” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”.

    It has been revealed that “The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”.

    Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers remarked they doubted very much would come from it.

    Recent findings suggest that “I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

    Recent findings suggest that “I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”.

    In a recent development, sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

    “Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal remarked Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”.

    Industry observers note that on spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to rapidly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

    “You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”.

    According to recent reports, john M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.

    #99858. Delta Is My Preferred Airline Of The “Major Three” US Carriers (Hear Me Out)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1300 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Delta Is My Preferred Airline Of The “Major Three” US Carriers (Hear Me Out)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, I’ve never been one to take the easy road, so I thought I’d bite the bullet and talk about my love for Delta in what you might call a baptism of fire.
    • This year, Delta has nudged up to fourth most-flown of the 94 airlines I’ve tried out over the years, and I’d like to share a little bit about why.
    • Starting from the ground, I am a significant fan of what Delta is doing with its lounges.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, I’ve never been one to take the easy road, so I thought I’d bite the bullet and talk about my love for Delta in what you might call a baptism of fire. Before I jump in, I’m not here screaming that Delta is the best US airline. Far from it. Rather, I’m explaining why, as someone who is not based in the US, Delta is my go-to airline.

    This year, Delta has nudged up to fourth most-flown of the 94 airlines I’ve tried out over the years, and I’d like to share a little bit about why.

    Starting from the ground, I am a significant fan of what Delta is doing with its lounges. Stepping inside one of Delta’s newer Sky Clubs, you feel like you’re in the lobby bar of a luxury hotel rather than the corporate canteen-style spaces offered by competitors.

    I know these newer lounges aren’t in every airport yet — Honolulu (HNL) is a notable exception — but lately I’ve found myself enjoying them before the majority of my latest Delta flights departing from a US airport.

    Don’t get me started on the Delta One Lounges: I’ve visited locations at LAX and JFK, and these are without a doubt my favorite airline lounges in the US.

    Stepping onboard, I actually like the planes. In recent times, I’ve flown mainly on its Airbus A320 family aircraft, a few Boeing 757s (which I love), and once on a Boeing 767-300 from Honolulu to LAX.

    I like how they’ve all had seatback screens, I’ve never had an issue using my SkyMiles account to access the fast free WiFi (it’s decent, even though it’s not Starlink), and I’ve never felt uncomfortable on one of Delta’s planes.

    I also have to say, I’ve always had pleasant, if not better-than-your-average service when flying Delta.

    Industry observers note that I love a good redemption as much as the next frequent flyer. However, our credit cards in the UK earn us far fewer points than those in the US, so for me, redeeming points is the exception, not the norm.

    As such, I don’t hate on Delta’s SkyMiles for its mostly sky-high redemption rates. Even if finding a one-way in Delta One from Rio or São Paulo to Latest York for less than 470,000 miles is almost impossible.

    Besides, I credit my Delta flights to my Flying Blue account, which is therefore home to my SkyTeam elite status and miles earned on Delta and all other SkyTeam airlines.

    Neither do I fly often enough nor have the funds to unlock top-tier status in all three alliances. Aside from the Virgin Atlantic Gold status I got from a status match and my BA Silver, which expires in April, Flying Blue is the only program whose status I’m actively chasing.

    As a direct result of Air France and KLM’s membership in the SkyTeam alliance, I actively choose to fly other SkyTeam airlines, such as Delta. Also, thanks to the relationship between Delta and fellow SkyTeam member Aeroméxico, I’ve managed to find great-value cash fares on several occasions when planning travel between Mexico and Canada or the US.

    I actually used to be a die-hard American boy until the BA Club was sabotaged. In terms of lounges, aircraft comfort, complimentary amenities (like seat back screens and Wi-Fi), and service, Delta has felt like an upgrade.

    For what it’s worth, if status had nothing to do with it, I’d still choose Delta.

    It has been revealed that my experience with American, Delta, and United has mainly been on domestic flights around the US, including transcons. In fact, I’ve never flown Delta One, American Flagship, or United Polaris on long-haul international flights. Who knows, my top three could reshuffle once I’ve tried and tested each of those. Maybe I’ll have to have a word with Ben about this….

    I know Delta gets a bad rep, but honestly I have only had pleasant experiences when flying the airline over the years. As long as I’m being loyal to SkyTeam, it will remain my preference when traveling to or around the US (unless it’s from the UK; then I’m team Virgin).

    US Army Moves To Restart Washington DC Helicopter Training Flights 2 Years After Deadly Crash

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the US Army is moving to resume helicopter training flights in airspace near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) as soon as the week of December 6, according to a recent report by Politico.
    • Training operations in the corridor were halted in May 2025 after an Army Black Hawk came too close to Reagan National and forced approaching commercial airliners to abort landings.
    • In a recent development, existing FAA regulations explicitly exclude routine training from essential flight categories in the restricted zone around Reagan National.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the US Army is moving to resume helicopter training flights in airspace near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) as soon as the week of December 6, according to a recent report by Politico. That timeline comes less than two years after the January 29, 2025 midair collision between an Army Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk and a PSA Airlines regional jet operating as American Airlines Flight 5342 over the Potomac River, a disaster that killed all 67 people aboard both aircraft.

    Training operations in the corridor were halted in May 2025 after an Army Black Hawk came too close to Reagan National and forced approaching commercial airliners to abort landings. Resuming training requires Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approval, and the service had not yet filed a formal request with regulators even as military officials briefed congressional staff on their plans.

    In a recent development, existing FAA regulations explicitly exclude routine training from essential flight categories in the restricted zone around Reagan National. Under interim final rule 2026-01226, which took effect on January 23, 2026, and permanently closed Helicopter Route 4 between Hains Point and the Wilson Bridge, only rare essential flights may enter designated airspace up to 1,500 feet (457 meters) mean sea level. Those narrow exceptions cover lifesaving medical missions, active law enforcement responses to ongoing crimes, national defense or counterintelligence operations, continuity of government, and transport of the President or Vice President.

    In a recent development, the rule specifies that proficiency evaluations, routine training, and non-essential personnel transport do not qualify as essential operations. Because the regulation bars routine training inside the designated Potomac zone, military leaders would need either a formal regulatory modification or an approved authorization pathway before standard pilot currency missions resume. FAA officials opened public comment on the interim rule through February 23, 2026, and indicated a final rule would follow after reviewing submissions, eliminated visual separation within five nautical miles (9.3 km) of the airport, increased staffing and oversight, and required air traffic controllers to manage commercial runway use when essential vertical-lift aircraft enter restricted airspace.

    Recent findings suggest that investigations by the National Transportation Safety Board and the Army traced the January 2025 collision to overlapping operational, technical, and airspace vulnerabilities rather than a single error. National Transportation Safety Board findings and reporting by Task & Purpose highlighted tight vertical margins near low-altitude river routes, radio frequency congestion, altimeter instrumentation discrepancies, and bright urban lighting that complicated visual detection at night.

    Sources indicate that investigators also noted that radio transmissions that might have helped crews confirm visual separation were missed or complicated by overlapping traffic. The National Transportation Safety Board issued 50 safety recommendations, including eight directed at the Army, and concluded that an Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast system could have alerted the airliner crew 59 seconds before impact. In response, the Army conducted fleet inspections, tested altimeters across Black Hawk variants, and reviewed crew separation procedures. These technical and procedural reviews reflect a broader effort to pair airframe checks with stricter altitude discipline across congested metropolitan corridors.

    Sources indicate that pushback from aviation labor unions and pending legislation on Capitol Hill complicate the Army's push for a December restart. Association of Flight Attendants president Sara Nelson condemned intends to bring military training back near Reagan National so soon after the fatal crash.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, lawmakers remain divided over final statutory mandates governing shared airspace and traffic-alerting equipment. According to The Washington Sun and Senate Commerce Committee reporting, the Rotor Operations Transparency and Oversight Reform Act passed the Senate unanimously in December 2025 but stalled in the House, though leaders revealed an agreement in principle in mid-November 2026 on a framework to reconcile competing bills before the end of the year. Negotiations involving the House Armed Services Committee remain central to settling how military helicopters and fixed-wing planes share crowded corridors, while commuters and airlines watch whether flight delays or runway adjustments could return. While Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell push to finish the legislation, unresolved details over military aircraft equipment requirements continue to draw scrutiny from safety advocates and families of the victims.

    • Dan McLaughlin is a senior writer at National Review Online and a fellow at National Review Institute.

    Recent findings suggest that populism, for all of its faults, can be a powerful force in politics when it is rising. While populist agendas can come in many different varieties, they are all propelled by a broad sense that the people — or more properly, The People — are being held back by some elite force, whether that be Major Business or an insular political establishment or something darker. If only we can overcome the enemy, we are told, we will sweep to victory on the broad, sunny uplands.

    Recent findings suggest that as I’ve noted before, the very nature of populism is that it has to redefine The People to include something less than all the people when it inevitably encounters the reality that its premises are not universally shared. And so it goes from there, because populism always sooner or later must decide to cling to its narratives when forced to choose between them and empirical reality:.

    Dan McLaughlin is a senior writer at National Review Online and a fellow at National Review Institute.

    #99855. When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1485 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1485 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, to push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question.
    • According to recent reports, every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those).
    • Sources indicate that the flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, to push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question. I’ll share my take, and then I’m curious to hear how OMAAT readers feel. Let’s start with some background, and then we’ll discuss best practices….

    According to recent reports, every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those). The flight attendant call button, is, as the name suggests, a way to call a flight attendant to your seat.

    Sources indicate that the flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service. However, that’s not how all flight attendants interpret it, so I want to talk about that in a bit more detail.

    Sources indicate that in most of the world, the flight attendant call button seems to work as intended. It’s a useful way to call over a flight attendant, whether you want a drink refill, or there’s some sort of an emergency.

    Recent findings suggest that however, in the United States I’ve heard several flight attendants over the years announce that the call button is in fact the “emergency flight attendant call button,” advising passengers to only use it if absolutely necessary. Suffice to say that this kind of announcement isn’t approved by any airline.

    While people will often joke “well I’m happy you consider my drink request to be an emergency,” let’s talk about when it’s actually appropriate to use a flight attendant call button.

    Broadly speaking, it’s always appropriate to use the flight attendant call button for service in first & business class, especially on international airlines. You’re paying a premium for more service, and having an extra request on a long haul flight isn’t unreasonable.

    I’ll take it a step further — at top airlines, crews generally prefer that you push the call button rather than going to the galley with your request. Foreign carriers typically have thick curtains between the galley and the cabin, and you generally shouldn’t try to go into the flight attendant’s “space” without permission. They’d much rather come to you. They might be putting on some makeup or eating a meal, and don’t want to be caught off guard. So absolutely push the flight attendant call button — it’s the courteous thing to do.

    Industry observers note that I do want to mention just one caveat — try to be respectful of the overall service flow. For example, if a cabin has 50+ business class seats and the crew is doing service with a cart and is currently in the aisle, wait until they finish that round of service before pushing the call button again, unless there’s something you absolutely need.

    When it comes to using the call button, you can’t beat Emirates first class, where you can voice or video call the crew with any requests, without them even having to come to your seat.

    Industry observers note that it’s also interesting to observe the cultural differences between airlines when it comes to service approaches. For example, in Singapore Airlines first class I generally don’t push the flight attendant call button, since even on a long haul flight, a crew member seems to pass through the cabin every 10-15 minutes throughout the flight. The service is just so proactive that I don’t find it necessary.

    Cathay Pacific first class is exactly the opposite — the crews are spectacularly reactive. That might sound sarcastic, but it’s not. On Cathay Pacific you (hopefully) won’t see a flight attendant once between meal services without calling them, and that’s so that your privacy is maximized. But if you push the call button a flight attendant will cheerily appear within seconds.

    Sources indicate that of course those are both airlines known for great service. You have all kinds of other airlines where flight attendants make a habit of not passing through the cabin, and when they do they almost seem to look down, to avoid making eye contact.

    It has been revealed that using the flight attendant call button in economy is trickier. There’s nothing inherently wrong with it, but the staffing ratio in economy is different than in first & business class, and in many cases flight attendants have to walk a lot further to your seat. Also keep in mind that on long haul flights the crew has rest periods, reducing the staffing ratio even further.

    Personally I think there’s nothing wrong with using the call button in economy:.

    It has been revealed that that being mentioned, in economy I also think it’s more reasonable to stretch your legs and go to the galley yourself. Generally there’s a small setup with snacks and drinks, at least on long haul flights, so you can help yourself to that. Furthermore, in my experience flight attendants are typically “sitting in the open” more in economy than in business or first class, given that the volume of requests is greater.

    It has been revealed that the above are my general thoughts, though is the story any different on airlines in the United States? This accounts for the fact that:.

    On US airlines I’m generally a little more hesitant to use the call button. I see what kind of a vibe the crew gives me. In general I don’t mind pushing the call button in international first & business class on a US airline, while I avoid it on domestic flights. If I get the sense that the crew takes glitch with use of the call button, I of course won’t use it.

    Industry observers note that all airplane seats have individual flight attendant call buttons, though customs around using them seem to differ. In the United States, some flight attendants seem to think these buttons are just for emergencies, while outside the United States there are consistently no issues with using them for service.

    Where do you stand on using the flight attendant call button, and what has your experience been?

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S.
    • Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a newly introduced challenge: Attendance.
    • Industry observers note that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, said attendance is 'a great frustration.' (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a newly introduced challenge: Attendance.

    Industry observers note that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break. This, a day after House GOP leadership pulled a procedural rule vote when it was clear the vote might fall short because of GOP no-shows – and then canceled a planned Friday voting session.

    It has been revealed that the House has just 12 scheduled voting days left in the 119th Congress. And leaders who have at times struggled to ensure sufficient support for their agenda from the narrow majority now say they will work to make sure cases of senioritis don’t compound the problem, as both returning and nonreturning members have been part of the problem.

    Industry observers note that "Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Thursday. “We'll be addressing that with members.".

    “We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can't do that unless people are present at work, so that's our challenge,” Johnson continued.

    Of 13 roll call votes in the House since the midterms, all but one has had a double-digit number of no-demonstrates; for five of the 13, more than 30 members did not vote. The average number of members not voting has more than doubled since the midterm elections, compared to the final 13 roll call votes beforehand.

    Industry observers note that johnson has just a few more weeks before he steps out of the spotlight and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, takes over the GOP conference as minority leader. But his members are still counting on him to get them back to Washington.

    It has been revealed that “I think there's going to be some serious conversations over the phone, behind the scenes over the weekend,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, remarked. “We all took an oath of office. We have a sworn duty to be here. We're still being paid to be here, and you have to show up and do the job.”.

    And it's not just leadership that's frustrated with their missing colleagues this week.

    Industry observers note that “There is, no question,” Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., who narrowly won reelection, responded when asked whether there was frustration in the caucus over members' absences.

    “I don't know what you do with people that don't understand the concept of duty,” Harrigan remarked. “I mean, look, you signed up for a two-year term. You execute your two-year term, no matter what happens along the way politically. You have an obligation both to your constituency and to your country to be here, so the fact that they're not self-motivated to be here, I don't think that there's really much that you can do.”.

    Attendance has also been a bipartisan problem. A group of House Democrats, including members of leadership, faced harsh criticism from party activists for not returning to the chamber in time for a vote related to a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

    While Republican leadership grapples with the fallout from the party’s election losses earlier this month, lawmakers still face a slew of legislative items as Congress looks ahead to the holidays and a government shutdown looms.

    Many Republicans want to see a party-line defense spending bill cross the finish line, while the NDAA remains in treacherous territory and Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has been dark for months.

    However, the frustration does not lie solely with absent House members.

    “The Senate needs to do their job,” Rep. John McGuire, R-Va., said. “I know we had a hard time in the midterms. History doesn't favor the party in the president's office, but we passed the Save America Act five times here. It goes over there, nothing. We've got a farm bill, nothing. We got an NDAA. We got so many things.”.

That means if you pay with an IHG credit card, you wouldn’t earn any bonus rewards, so it’s not treated as if it’s IHG spending.

    Therefore I’d recommend using a card on which you’re trying to reach a minimum spending requirement, or otherwise, a credit card that maximizes your return on everyday spending. See this post for more on which credit cards are best for buying points.

    Sources indicate that IHG One Rewards has dynamic award pricing, which means there’s no minimum or maximum number of points a hotel stay can cost. Rather, the cost of an award stay generally correlates somewhat to the cost of a revenue stay.

    However, that doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll get the same value with all hotel stays. There are many situations where you can get outsized value by buying points and then redeeming them. Let me just give a few examples, using stays I pulled up for random dates (again, pricing is dynamic, so this won’t reflect what you see every day).

    For example, the Six Senses Kyoto is bookable for 165,000 points per night, and you could purchase those points for $825.

    That represents massive savings over the cash cost, which is $1,493.

    On the other end of the spectrum, the Holiday Inn Express & Suites Tampa is bookable for 33,000 points per night, and you could purchase those points for $165.

    That represents massive savings over the cash cost, which is $230.

    However, this won’t always be a good deal. For example, take the Kimpton Tres Rios in Playa del Carmen is bookable for 104,000 points per night, and you could purchase those points for $520.

    That’s not a good deal compared to the cash cost, which is $429, so there you’d be better off just paying cash directly.

    Another thing to keep in mind is that select IHG co-branded credit cards offer free night awards, and those are worth up to a certain number of points. What’s great is that these free night awards can typically be topped off with points, so there could be merit to buying IHG points so that you have points with which to top off these certificates.

    You’ll get the most value from your IHG points if you have The Brand New IHG One Rewards Premier Select Credit Card (learn more), The New IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card (learn more), and The New IHG One Rewards Business Credit Card (learn more).

    According to recent reports, that’s because the cards offer a fourth night free benefit, meaning that you can book a four night award stay for the cost of three nights. This is essentially the equivalent of 25% off in increments of four nights, since you can use this benefit an unlimited number of times.

    Sources indicate that just to use the Six Senses Kyoto example above, if you earned 495,000 points (worth $2,475 at 0.5 cents per point), that would be enough for four nights with the fourth night free. That represents an absolutely massive discount.

    IHG has over 15 hotel brands, so there are lots of options for redeeming your IHG One Rewards points. IHG points can be redeemed at the following properties, among others:.

    Everyone will value points differently. Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider IHG points to be worth 0.5 cents each, and I tend to value points pretty conservatively. So the purchase price is around what I value these points.

    Sources indicate that for non-elite members, IHG One Rewards points expire after 12 months of inactivity. However, any sort of points earning or redemption activity would reset the expiration of your points. Furthermore, IHG One Rewards points don’t expire for elite members in the program.

    Keep in mind that IHG elite status is quite easy to earn. Just for having The Brand Latest IHG One Rewards Premier Select Credit Card (learn more) or The New IHG One Rewards Business Credit Card (learn more), you receive Platinum status, without any sort of a spending requirement.

    IHG One Rewards doesn’t have blackout dates on award nights, but the program does have capacity controls. What this means is that some number of standard rooms will be made available for award redemptions every night, but that doesn’t mean that all standard rooms are available for award redemptions.

    According to recent reports, IHG One Rewards is offering a sale on purchased points. Through December 11, 2026, IHG One Rewards is offering a promotion, and members seem to be eligible for a 100% bonus, which is an opportunity to buy points for 0.5 cents each.

    There are instances where buying points can save you over 50% on the cost of a luxury hotel stay. I also think there’s value in having a “reserve” of IHG points, given the brand’s global footprint. You can get even more value out of buying IHG points in conjunction with a premium IHG credit card, so you can get a fourth night free on award redemptions.

    Do you plan on buying IHG points with a bonus?

    According to recent reports, membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

    America’s leading natural gas competitor is on track to become its biggest customer. With traffic down through the Strait of Hormuz, Qatar is betting on U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG). The state’s energy company, QatarEnergy, signed two purchase agreements for American LNG in late October and is reportedly in talks with U.S. supplier Venture Global for a third. There may yet be more deals coming down the pike, including one with Houston-based NextDecade. QatarEnergy already owns 70 percent of Golden Pass LNG, a joint venture with ExxonMobil that shipped its first cargo out of Sabine Pass, Texas, in April.

    Sources indicate that doha’s ventures are adding up. So much so that, according to an early November Financial Times report, Qatar may become “the biggest U.S. LNG buyer” by 2033. This presents the United States with opportunities to affirm market leadership and drive a wedge between Doha and Tehran.

    In a recent development, natalie Ecanow is a research analyst for the Foundation for the Defense of Democracies. Her work focuses on the Middle East.

    #99849. Delta Air Lines Thought It Remarked Goodbye To Queen Of The Skies Until It Had No Choice But To Fly It Again 31 Years Later
